basis: case strength: distinct families backing the selection (a family contributes at most one, so near-duplicate systems cannot manufacture agreement), then how much of the genome's own mechanism claim fired and at what threshold rung, then board depth and freshness, then price standing as the final tiebreak. Price standing is execution quality and never predictive merit: the consensus is derived from the same prices, so their difference can never be evidence the market is wrong.

picks.evidence_tier_label: More than one system agrees, or one system's signal cleared its hardest threshold.
picks.thesis: Backing the away side of h2h because 1 pre-registered signal fired: (1) starter_groundball_share -- the opposing starter's career ground-ball share (each side's number describes the matchup that side's own lineup faces): away 36.9%, home 61.4% (this game's own values rest on: away over 176 batted balls; home over 1,563 batted balls); a gap of 24.5 percentage points, clearing the threshold of 17.5 percentage points (rung 3 of 3, the 90th percentile of that gap over the ladder's derivation sample, 3,516 games with both sides measured, 2023-24). This mechanism's direction was frozen before any search ran at -1 (the side holding more of it is the side the mechanism harms), so the signal points to the away side. Pre-registered reason it should matter: a career ground-ball starter takes the air out of an offence that lives on balls in the air, so the lineup facing the higher ground-ball share is the disadvantaged side and club-level pricing averages the collision out. This is a signal count, not a forecast: the genome publishes no calibrated probability, so p_model is null and edge_bps is null by construction. Nothing here says the market's price is mistaken, and no claim of value is attached to it -- no such claim has been earned (docs/PREREG_CALIBRATED_PROBABILITY.md). (Strategy: evolab genome 606be696ff199952.)
